subproblem.title: Scalar weight controlled by the multivector difference via a norming covector
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For an n-covector α on ℝ^P (an element of Covector (Euclid P) n, i.e. a continuous alternating map), let ‖α‖ be its operator norm and |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α its Euclidean coefficient norm. MultiVector P n = Λ_n(ℝ^P) is the space of continuous linear functionals on n-covectors, with operator norm ‖·‖ and [0,∞]-valued norm ‖·‖ₑ. Let ζx, ζa ∈ MultiVector P n and t, t₀, C ∈ ℝ with t₀ ≥ 0 and C ≥ 0. Assume ‖α‖ ≤ C·|α| and |ζa(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α, and that there is an n-covector β with |β| ≤ 1 and ζx(β) = 1. Then, in [0,∞], ofReal t ≤ ofReal t₀ + ofReal C · ‖t•ζx − t₀•ζa‖ₑ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ζx ζa : MultiVector P n) (t t₀ C : ℝ), 0 ≤ t₀ → 0 ≤ C → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ‖α‖ ≤ C * covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ζa α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ 1 ∧ ζx β = 1) → ENNReal.ofReal t ≤ ENNReal.ofReal t₀ + ENNReal.ofReal C * ‖t • ζx - t₀ • ζa‖ₑ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (fact F2) of the parent proof, with the operator-norm comparison ‖α‖ ≤ C|α| as a hypothesis.
Notation: |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm. For an n-covector α, ‖α‖ is its operator norm as a continuous alternating map. For d ∈ MultiVector P n = (Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ), ‖d‖ is the operator norm and ‖d‖ₑ = ofReal ‖d‖.
1. By hypothesis, choose an n-covector β with |β| ≤ 1 and ζx(β) = 1. Put d := t•ζx − t₀•ζa ∈ MultiVector P n.
2. Evaluating a continuous linear map at β is linear in the map (ContinuousLinearMap.sub_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul). So d(β) = t·ζx(β) − t₀·ζa(β) = t − t₀·ζa(β).
3. By le_abs_self and the hypothesis on ζa, ζa(β) ≤ |ζa(β)| ≤ |β| ≤ 1. Since t₀ ≥ 0, t₀·ζa(β) ≤ t₀ (mul_le_of_le_one_right).
4. By the comparison hypothesis, ‖β‖ ≤ C·|β|. Since C ≥ 0 and |β| ≤ 1, C·|β| ≤ C (mul_le_of_le_one_right). Hence ‖β‖ ≤ C.
5. We have d(β) ≤ |d(β)| = ‖d(β)‖ ≤ ‖d‖·‖β‖ by ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm applied to d at β. By step 4 and ‖d‖ ≥ 0 (norm_nonneg d, mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left), this is ≤ ‖d‖·C = C·‖d‖.
6. By step 2, t = d(β) + t₀·ζa(β). Steps 5 and 3 then give t ≤ C‖d‖ + t₀, i.e. t ≤ t₀ + C‖d‖ (linarith).
7. ENNReal.ofReal is monotone (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal), so ofReal t ≤ ofReal(t₀ + C‖d‖). Since t₀ ≥ 0 and C‖d‖ ≥ 0 (mul_nonneg with norm_nonneg d), ENNReal.ofReal_add gives ofReal(t₀ + C‖d‖) = ofReal t₀ + ofReal(C‖d‖). Since C ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_mul gives ofReal(C‖d‖) = ofReal C · ofReal‖d‖. Finally ofReal‖d‖ = ‖d‖ₑ by ofReal_norm d (ofReal_norm_eq_enorm is its deprecated alias). Hence ofReal t ≤ ofReal t₀ + ofReal C · ‖t•ζx − t₀•ζa‖ₑ. ∎
Lean remark: the norm on MultiVector P n elaborates as ContinuousLinearMap.hasOpNorm. Generic lemmas unify with it when the element is given explicitly (norm_nonneg d, ofReal_norm d, d.le_opNorm β). With an implicit argument, `rw [ofReal_norm]` does not find its pattern.
proof_key_steps: Pick the norming covector β of ζx (|β| ≤ 1, ζx(β) = 1) and set d := t•ζx − t₀•ζa, so that d(β) = t − t₀·ζa(β).
t₀·ζa(β) ≤ t₀, from ζa(β) ≤ |ζa(β)| ≤ |β| ≤ 1 and t₀ ≥ 0.
d(β) ≤ ‖d‖·‖β‖ ≤ C‖d‖, by le_opNorm and ‖β‖ ≤ C|β| ≤ C.
Hence t ≤ t₀ + C‖d‖; then ofReal_add, ofReal_mul and ofReal_norm give the [0,∞] form.

audit.reason: The prose includes every hypothesis and matches the standalone one-line proposition. Evaluating the difference at the norming covector, using t₀,C ≥ 0, and applying the operator-norm bound gives t ≤ t₀ + C‖d‖. The stated ofReal conversions prove the exact conclusion even for negative t. The proof is complete and non-circular; its fresh bare name is valid.
